foods.description: WHO lists whole grains such as oats, millet and brown rice among healthy sources of carbohydrates. This is general education, not a food prescription for a dosha or health condition.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: Carbohydrates in the diet should come primarily from whole grains, vegetables, fruits and pulses.

foods.description: WHO lists pulses such as lentils, chickpeas, beans and dried peas among healthy carbohydrate sources. Choose varieties and preparation that fit your dietary practice and personal needs.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: Examples of pulses include lentils, chickpeas, beans, and dried peas.

foods.food: Fruit (fresh, frozen or canned without added sugar)
foods.description: WHO includes fruit in a varied healthy diet and notes that fresh, frozen or canned fruit can be suitable when canned options have no added sugars or excess sodium.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: Fresh fruit and vegetables are great choices but frozen and canned are also good, provided they don’t have added sugars or excess sodium.

foods.food: Vegetables (fresh, frozen or canned without excess sodium)
foods.description: WHO includes vegetables in a varied healthy diet and notes that fresh, frozen or canned vegetables can be suitable when canned options have no added sugars or excess sodium.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: Fresh fruit and vegetables are great choices but frozen and canned are also good, provided they don’t have added sugars or excess sodium.

foods.food: Sugary drinks and foods with added sugars
foods.description: WHO recommends limiting free sugars. This is broad public-health information, not an individualized restriction.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: The consumption of free sugars should be limited throughout the life course.

foods.food: Packaged snacks high in salt or unhealthy fats
foods.description: WHO recommends limiting foods high in unhealthy fats and salt. Check local labels because packaged foods vary.

source.title: WHO: Healthy diet
source.snippet: A variety of minimally processed and unprocessed foods low in unhealthy fats, free sugars and sodium are the foundation of any healthy diet.

routine.title: Build movement into your day
routine.description: Walking, cycling, active recreation and everyday movement all count as physical activity. Choose an amount and activity that feel comfortable for you.

source.title: WHO: Physical activity
source.snippet: All movement including during leisure time, for transport to get to and from places, or as part of a person’s work or domestic activities.

routine.title: Break up long periods of sitting
routine.description: Look for comfortable opportunities to stand or move during the day. WHO advises people of all age groups to limit sedentary time.

source.title: WHO: Physical activity
source.snippet: All age groups should limit the amount of time being sedentary.

routine.title: Keep a regular sleep and wake schedule
routine.description: CDC lists going to bed and getting up at the same time each day as a sleep habit that can support good sleep.

source.title: CDC: About sleep
source.snippet: Going to bed and getting up at the same time every day.

routine.title: Put screens away before bedtime
routine.description: CDC suggests turning off electronic devices at least 30 minutes before bedtime as one sleep habit.

source.title: CDC: About sleep
source.snippet: Turning off electronic devices at least 30 minutes before bedtime.
